newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian PM Gujral cancels Malaysia, Singapore visit.
newsitem.headline: Indian PM Gujral cancels Malaysia, Singapore visit.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral has cancelled visits to Malaysia and Singapore due to start on July 26, a Foreign Ministry spokesman said on Wednesday.
"The Indian delegation to the ASEAN Regional Forum meeting in Kuala Lumpur will now be headed by the finance minister, P. Chidambaram," the spokesman told Reuters.
He said Gujral, who is also foreign minister, would be busy with domestic political issues. July 29 is the deadline for filing nominations for vice-presidential elections in India.
The Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) Regional Forum is holding a meeting of foreign ministers from July 26 to 29, to which India has been invited.
ASEAN comprises Indonesia, Thailand, the Philippines, Malaysia, Singapore, Vietnam and Brunei.
After the meeting in Kuala Lumpur, Gujral was scheduled to visit Singapore for a day before returning to India.
Gujral's United Front coalition was rocked on Monday by an announcement by a member, the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK), that it planned to pull out of the government.
Four of Gujral's ministers are part of the DMK.
The choice of a vice-presidential candidate by United Front members is regarded as test of Gujral's leadership and a measure of the coalition's unity.
